title: If the ideal of a presentation is generated by a regular sequence at a prime, the algebra is a global complete intersection near that prime
statement: Let $k$ be a field, $n\ge0$, $P=k[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ the polynomial ring [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring], $I\subseteq P$ an ideal, $S=P/I$, $\mathfrak q\subset S$ a prime ideal and $\mathfrak q'\subset P$ its inverse image under $P\to S$. Let $P_{\mathfrak q'}$ be the localization of $P$ at $\mathfrak q'$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] and $IP_{\mathfrak q'}$ the ideal of $P_{\mathfrak q'}$ generated by the elements $f/1$, $f\in I$. Assume that there are an integer $e\ge0$ and elements $h_1,\dots,h_e\in P_{\mathfrak q'}$ which form a regular sequence in $P_{\mathfrak q'}$ [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence] and generate the ideal $IP_{\mathfrak q'}$. Then there is $g\in S$ with $g\notin\mathfrak q$ such that the localization $S_g$ [def-weil-ring-localization-away] is a global complete intersection over $k$ [def-weil-pbc-complete-intersection-over-field].

source.place: Algebra, Lemma 00SC (label lemma-lci, line 35909), implication (5) => (1): proof, second paragraph ((5) => (2): e = c = height(q') - height(q) by dimension theory) and third paragraph ((2) => (1): clearing denominators f_i' = d_i f_i, g' with I_{g'} = (f_1',...,f_c'), g'' with dim S_{g''} = dim_q Spec S = n - c by Lemma 00P2 lemma-codimension, S_g = k[x_1..x_{n+1}]/(f_1',...,f_c', x_{n+1}g'g'' - 1))

proof.text: (Setup.) Let $\pi:P\to S=P/I$ be the quotient map; then $\mathfrak q'=\pi^{-1}(\mathfrak q)$ is a prime ideal of $P$ with $I\subseteq\mathfrak q'$. The field $k$ is Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] (its only ideals are $0$ and $k$), so $P=k[x_1,\dots,x_n]/(0)$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring] is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian]; hence $I=(u_1,\dots,u_m)$ for some $m\ge0$ and $u_1,\dots,u_m\in I$. Put $U=P\setminus\mathfrak q'$ and $R=P_{\mathfrak q'}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], a local ring with maximal ideal $\mathfrak q'R$, and Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian] (with $R'=R$, the map $p\mapsto p/1$). Bringing a finite sum $\sum_i(r_i/w_i)(f_i/1)$ ($f_i\in I$, $w_i\in U$) to the common denominator $w=\prod_iw_i\in U$ shows $IR=\{f/w: f\in I,\ w\in U\}$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00SC (label lemma-lci, line 35909), proof, second paragraph ((5) => (2)), first sentence of the first paragraph (R = k[x_1,...,x_n]_{q'}) and third paragraph (finite generation implicit in the choice of g')

proof.text: ($R/IR\cong S_{\mathfrak q}$; the source's $\overline R=R/IR=S_{\mathfrak q}$.) Since $\mathfrak q'=\pi^{-1}(\mathfrak q)$, $\pi(U)\subseteq S\setminus\mathfrak q$, so $\rho:R\to S_{\mathfrak q}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], $p/w\mapsto\pi(p)/\pi(w)$, is well defined (if $p/w=p'/w'$, i.e. $v(pw'-p'w)=0$ with $v\in U$, apply $\pi$) and a ring homomorphism. It is surjective: an element $s/t$ of $S_{\mathfrak q}$ has $s=\pi(p)$, $t=\pi(w)$ with $w\notin\mathfrak q'$ as $\pi(w)\notin\mathfrak q$. Its kernel is $IR$: an element $f/w$ with $f\in I$ maps to $0$; conversely, if $\pi(p)/\pi(w)=0$ there is $t=\pi(v)\in S\setminus\mathfrak q$, so $v\in U$, with $\pi(vp)=0$, i.e. $vp\in I$, and then $p/w=vp/(vw)\in IR$ by step 1. Hence $\rho$ induces a ring isomorphism $R/IR\cong S_{\mathfrak q}$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00SC (label lemma-lci, line 35909), proof, first paragraph ('R/IR = R/I_{q'} = S_q')

proof.text: ($\dim R/IR+e=\dim R$; 'dimension theory'.) For $0\le i\le e$ let $J_i=(h_1,\dots,h_i)\subseteq R$ and $R_i=R/J_i$ (so $R_0=R$). By [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence], (1) multiplication by $h_i$ on $R/J_{i-1}=R_{i-1}$ is injective, i.e. the class $\bar h_i\in R_{i-1}$ is a nonzerodivisor of the ring $R_{i-1}$, and (2) $R_e=R/J_e\neq0$. Every $h_i$ lies in $\mathfrak q'R$: otherwise $h_i$ is a unit of the local ring $R$ and $J_e=R$, contradicting (2). Each $R_i$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-image-noetherian] (step 1), nonzero (it surjects onto $R_e\neq0$), and local with maximal ideal $\mathfrak q'R/J_i$ (an element of $R_i$ outside it is the class of a unit of $R$); $\bar h_i\in R_{i-1}$ lies in the maximal ideal $\mathfrak q'R/J_{i-1}$, and $R_{i-1}/\bar h_iR_{i-1}\cong R/(J_{i-1}+h_iR)=R_i$. By [lem-weil-pbc-dimension-quotient-nonzerodivisor] applied to the Noetherian local ring $R_{i-1}$ and the nonzerodivisor $\bar h_i$, $\dim R_i+1=\dim R_{i-1}$ (Krull dimensions [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring], a ring isomorphism preserving them). Adding these $e$ equalities, $\dim R_e+e=\dim R$. Since $h_1,\dots,h_e$ generate $IR$, $J_e=IR$ and $\dim(R/IR)+e=\dim R$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00SC (label lemma-lci, line 35909), proof, second paragraph ((5) => (2)): dim(S_q) = dim(k[x_1,...,x_n]_{q'}) - e 'by dimension theory, see Section section-dimension' (line 14306); the fact used is Lemma Tag 00KW (label lemma-one-equation, line 14694) for a nonzerodivisor, applied e times

proof.text: ($e=\operatorname{ht}(\mathfrak q')-\operatorname{ht}(\mathfrak q)$ and $\dim_{\mathfrak q}\operatorname{Spec}S=n-e$.) Write $\operatorname{ht}$ for the supremum of the lengths of chains of primes ending inside the given prime, as in [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-quotient-dimension-at-point-height-difference]. By [lem-weil-pbc-localization-dimension-chains-below-prime], $\dim R=\dim P_{\mathfrak q'}=\operatorname{ht}(\mathfrak q')$ and $\dim S_{\mathfrak q}=\operatorname{ht}(\mathfrak q)$ [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]; by step 2 (a ring isomorphism preserves Krull dimension) $\dim(R/IR)=\operatorname{ht}(\mathfrak q)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-quotient-dimension-at-point-height-difference] both heights are integers in $[0,n]$ and $\dim_{\mathfrak q}(\operatorname{Spec}S)=n-\operatorname{ht}(\mathfrak q')+\operatorname{ht}(\mathfrak q)$ [def-kun-topological-dimension-at-point]. Step 3 gives $\operatorname{ht}(\mathfrak q)+e=\operatorname{ht}(\mathfrak q')$, an equality of integers, so $e=\operatorname{ht}(\mathfrak q')-\operatorname{ht}(\mathfrak q)$ (the source's $c$) and $d:=\dim_{\mathfrak q}(\operatorname{Spec}S)=n-e$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00SC (label lemma-lci, line 35909), proof, second paragraph ((5) => (2)) ('height(q) = dim(S_q) = dim(k[x_1,...,x_n]_{q'}) - e = height(q') - e ... We conclude that e = c'), with c = height(q') - height(q), i.e. dim_q(S) = n - c, from the statement of 00SC and Lemma Tag 00P2 (lemma-codimension, line 28270)

proof.text: (Clearing denominators.) Each $h_i\in IR$, so by step 1 $h_i=f_i'/s_i$ with $f_i'\in I$ and $s_i\in U$. Then $f_i'/1=(s_i/1)h_i$ with $s_i/1$ a unit of $R$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], so the elements $f_1'/1,\dots,f_e'/1$ generate the same ideal of $R$ as $h_1,\dots,h_e$, namely $IR$. Let $F=(f_1',\dots,f_e')\subseteq P$; $F\subseteq I$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00SC (label lemma-lci, line 35909), proof, third paragraph ((2) => (1)): 'we may find d_i not in q' such that f_i' = d_i f_i in k[x_1,...,x_n]. Then it is still true that I_{q'} = (f_1',...,f_c')R'

proof.text: (The element $g'$: $g'I\subseteq F$.) For each generator $u_j$ of $I$ (step 1), $u_j/1\in IR=(f_1'/1,\dots,f_e'/1)$ (step 5); bringing the coefficients to a common denominator, $u_j/1=\big(\sum_lc_{jl}f_l'\big)/t_j$ with $c_{jl}\in P$, $t_j\in U$. By the definition of equality in $R=P_{\mathfrak q'}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] there is $w_j\in U$ with $w_j\big(t_ju_j-\sum_lc_{jl}f_l'\big)=0$, so $v_ju_j\in F$ for $v_j=w_jt_j\in U$. Put $g'=\prod_{j=1}^mv_j$ ($g'=1$ if $m=0$); $g'\in U$, i.e. $g'\notin\mathfrak q'$, as $\mathfrak q'$ is prime. Then $g'u_j\in F$ for all $j$, and since $I=\sum_jPu_j$, $g'I\subseteq F$; with $F\subseteq I$ this is the source's $I_{g'}=(f_1',\dots,f_e')$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00SC (label lemma-lci, line 35909), proof, third paragraph ((2) => (1)): 'Hence there exists a g' not in q' such that I_{g'} = (f_1',...,f_c')'

proof.text:
(The element $g''$ and $g$.) Let $X=\operatorname{Spec}S$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] and $d=n-e$ as in step 4. By [def-kun-topological-dimension-at-point], $d$ is the minimum of $\dim U'$ over the open neighbourhoods $U'$ of $\mathfrak q$; let $U_0$ be one with $\dim U_0=d$. The closed subsets of $X$ are the sets $V(J)=\{\mathfrak p:J\subseteq\mathfrak p\}$, $J\subseteq S$ an ideal [lem-weil-pbc-spec-irreducible-closed-subsets-primes], so $U_0=X\setminus V(J)$ for some $J$, and $\mathfrak q\in U_0$ gives $\gamma\in J$ with $\gamma
otin\mathfrak q$. Then $D(\gamma)=\{\mathfrak p:\gamma
otin\mathfrak p\}\subseteq U_0$ (if $\gamma
otin\mathfrak p$ then $J
ot\subseteq\mathfrak p$). Choose $g''\in P$ with $\pi(g'')=\gamma$; $g''
otin\mathfrak q'$. Put $G=g'g''\in P$ and $g=\pi(G)\in S$. Since $\pi(g')
otin\mathfrak q$ (step 6, $\mathfrak q'=\pi^{-1}(\mathfrak q)$), $\gamma
otin\mathfrak q$ and $\mathfrak q$ is prime, $g
otin\mathfrak q$, i.e. $\mathfrak q\in D(g)$; and $D(g)\subseteq D(\gamma)\subseteq U_0$, since $g
otin\mathfrak p$ implies $\gamma
otin\mathfrak p$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00SC (label lemma-lci, line 35909), proof, third paragraph ((2) => (1)): 'pick g'' not in q' such that dim(S_{g''}) = dim_q Spec(S) ... set g equal to the image of g'g'' in S'; the existence of g'' is the remark after Topology Definition Tag 0055 (topology.tex, label definition-Krull, line 1392; remark line 1421: x has a fundamental system of open neighbourhoods U with dim(U) = dim_x(X)), written out with principal opens

proof.text: ($\dim S_g=n-e$.) $D(g)$ is an open neighbourhood of $\mathfrak q$ (step 7), so $\dim D(g)\ge d$ by the definition of $d=\dim_{\mathfrak q}X$ as a minimum [def-kun-topological-dimension-at-point]; and $D(g)\subseteq U_0$ are open in $X$, so $\dim D(g)\le\dim U_0=d$ by [lem-weil-pbc-open-subspace-dimension-monotone]. Hence $\dim D(g)=d=n-e$. By [lem-weil-pbc-principal-localization-open-immersion] the morphism $\operatorname{Spec}S_g\to\operatorname{Spec}S$ induced by the localization map $S\to S_g$ [def-weil-ring-localization-away] is an open immersion with image $D(g)$, so a homeomorphism of $\operatorname{Spec}S_g$ onto the subspace $D(g)$; a homeomorphism maps strict chains of irreducible closed subsets bijectively onto strict chains of the same length, so the Krull dimension of the space $\operatorname{Spec}S_g$ [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension] is $\dim S_g=\dim D(g)=n-e$. In particular $S_g\neq0$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00SC (label lemma-lci, line 35909), proof, third paragraph ((2) => (1)): 'by our choice of g'' this ring has dimension n - c'; monotonicity of dimension on open subsets from the remark after Topology Definition Tag 0055 (topology.tex line 1421: if U' subset U subset X are open then dim(U') <= dim(U)); Spec(S_g) = D(g) by Algebra Lemma Tag 00E4 (label lemma-standard-open)

proof.text: (The presentation.) Let $x=x_{n+1}$; by the universal property [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring] the $k$-algebra maps $k[x_1,\dots,x_{n+1}]\rightleftarrows P[x]$ fixing every $x_i$ are mutually inverse, so we identify $k[x_1,\dots,x_{n+1}]=P[x]$. Let $\pi_x:P[x]\to S[x]$ apply $\pi$ to the coefficients: it is surjective with kernel $IP[x]$ (the ideal generated by $I$) by [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-coefficient-map-kernel]. Let $\lambda:S[x]\to S_g$ be the $S$-algebra map with $\lambda(x)=1/g$; by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-away-polynomial-quotient] (with $R=S$, $r=g$; $S_g$ as in [def-weil-ring-localization-away]) $\lambda$ is surjective with kernel $(gx-1)S[x]$. So $\Phi=\lambda\circ\pi_x:k[x_1,\dots,x_{n+1}]\to S_g$ is a surjective homomorphism of $k$-algebras. Its kernel is $IP[x]+(Gx-1)P[x]$: $\pi_x(Gx-1)=gx-1$, so $\supseteq$ holds; if $\Phi(p)=0$ then $\pi_x(p)=(gx-1)\pi_x(p_0)$ for some $p_0\in P[x]$ ($\pi_x$ surjective), so $p-(Gx-1)p_0\in\ker\pi_x=IP[x]$. Let $K=(f_1',\dots,f_e',Gx-1)\subseteq P[x]$. Then $K\subseteq\ker\Phi$ as $f_i'\in I$ (step 5). Conversely, for $u\in I$: $u=-u(Gx-1)+xg''\cdot(g'u)$, and $g'u\in F$ by step 6, so $u\in K$; hence $IP[x]\subseteq K$ and $\ker\Phi=K$. Therefore $\Phi$ induces an isomorphism of $k$-algebras $k[x_1,\dots,x_{n+1}]/(f_1',\dots,f_e',\,x_{n+1}g'g''-1)\cong S_g$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00SC (label lemma-lci, line 35909), proof, third paragraph ((2) => (1)): 'S_g = k[x_1,...,x_n,x_{n+1}]/(f_1',...,f_c', x_{n+1}g'g'' - 1)', the isomorphism written out (S[x]/(gx-1) = S_g as in the proof of Lemma Tag 08JZ, line 35632)

proof.text: (Conclusion.) By step 9, $S_g\cong k[x_1,\dots,x_{n+1}]/(f_1',\dots,f_e',x_{n+1}g'g''-1)$ as $k$-algebras, a quotient of a polynomial ring in $n+1$ variables by $e+1$ polynomials, and by step 8 $\dim S_g=n-e=(n+1)-(e+1)$. By [def-weil-pbc-complete-intersection-over-field] (1), $S_g$ is a global complete intersection over $k$, and $g\notin\mathfrak q$ (step 7).

lean.statement: theorem exists_globalCompleteIntersection_of_regularSequence (k : Type u) [Field k] (n : ℕ) (I : Ideal (MvPolynomial (Fin n) k)) (q : Ideal (MvPolynomial (Fin n) k ⧸ I)) (hq : q.IsPrime) (e : ℕ) (h : Fin e → Localization.AtPrime (q.comap (Ideal.Quotient.mk I))) (hreg : RingTheory.Sequence.IsRegular (Localization.AtPrime (q.comap (Ideal.Quotient.mk I))) (List.ofFn h)) (hgen : Ideal.map (algebraMap (MvPolynomial (Fin n) k) (Localization.AtPrime (q.comap (Ideal.Quotient.mk I)))) I = Ideal.span (Set.range h)) : ∃ g : (MvPolynomial (Fin n) k ⧸ I), g ∉ q ∧ Algebra.IsGlobalCompleteIntersection k (Localization.Away g)
